memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "An owner who hits a male or female slave in the eye and destroys it must let the slave go free to compensate for the eye. And an owner who knocks out the tooth of a male or female slave must let the slave go free to compensate for the tooth." - Exodus 21:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once again God stands on the side of the vulnerable. A master who injured a servant — even in something as small as a knocked-out tooth — had to set that servant free. Cruelty carried a cost. The very violence meant to dominate became the servant's ticket to liberty. God turned the tables so that abuse led to release, not deeper bondage.

This is such a picture of how God works. He takes what was meant for harm and brings freedom out of it. The weak person, wounded and powerless, walks away free because God had written protection into the law on their behalf. No one could mistreat them without consequence. God noticed even a single tooth.

And this is the heart we meet fully in Jesus. He came "to proclaim freedom for the prisoners... to set the oppressed free" (Luke 4:18). He is drawn to the wounded, not repelled by them. If you have been hurt or beaten down by life or by others, take heart: the God of Scripture has always leaned toward the injured to lift them up. And He calls us never to use our strength to wound, but always to protect and release.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Have I used my strength to wound someone rather than to protect them?
How does God's care for the wounded encourage me if I feel beaten down?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You bring freedom out of wounds and care for the smallest hurt. Heal my wounds, and keep me from ever using my strength to harm those weaker than me. Amen.
